text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for model_variant=gpt-rw-13b-int8-stream in region=us-west-2. p99=2.6s (SLO=1.2s). Paging oncall @eric (severity=P2).

eric (oncall): ack — pulling metrics now. any immediate customer reports?

cs-bot: Customer-impact summary: 9 tickets in last 10m, 3 escalations (enterprise), multiple reports of streaming stalls and partial responses.

anya (sre): digging into infra traces — early signs: sudden increase in KV cache miss rate and longer step times in the dequant path. hitting the quant-pool-1 nodes. attaching quick snapshot: p95=850ms, p99=2600ms, error-rate ~0.4%. link: https://dash.internal/r/alerts/1765801234

rahul (ml-infra): FYI — we rolled a new int8 precision profile to canary yesterday 02:00 UTC (profile id: qprof-2026-03-12-v7). Canary was 5% traffic, but routing bump happened via autoscale test at 08:40 UTC and might have nudged more requests through quant nodes.

jess (runtime): logs from a quantized host:
```
[2026-03-15T14:15:12Z] quant_apply_scale(layer=14) WARN fallback to per-channel scaling
[2026-03-15T14:15:12Z] kv_cache_miss key=prefix:abcd latency=112ms
[2026-03-15T14:15:13Z] stall_detected stream_id=xyz stalled_for=3100ms
```

anya (sre): also seeing a pattern where long-context streaming requests trigger large KV lookups and the dequant path is occasionally blocking on a calibration retry. p99 spikes align with these long requests.

eric (oncall): can we triage quickly: 1) Is this limited to canary users? 2) Is rollback of qprof feasible? 3) Any short-term routing fix?

rahul (ml-infra): (1) Not limited — within 20m the canary routing mesh propagated to more hosts due to affinity-based placement; impact is currently ~12% of traffic hitting int8 nodes, but those nodes are hot. (2) Rollback is possible: qprof-2026-03-06-v3 is previous stable. I can trigger a profile rollback to baseline on the quant pool. That should reduce dequant errors.

jess (runtime): (3) Short-term: enable model_variant routing to fp16-stable for premium routes and enable graceful fallback for streaming:
```
# temp route cmd (admin)
route update --model gpt-rw-13b --policy "prefer:fp16-stable, fallback:int8" --scope=enterprise
```

anya (sre): Agree on both rollback + routing. Also increasing KV cache TTL for prefix keys should lower misses for hot long-context flows. I'll apply a TTL bump to 30s on kv-prefix cache.

luis (product): Heads up — enterprise customers on shared routes need immediate notice. CS to send an outbound with "we're mitigating a latency issue, mitigation in progress". Don't call it a rollback in customer comms.

cs-bot: Draft message prepared and queued for approval by @luis.

jess (runtime): triggering fp16 routing now for routes tagged premium and for streaming=true.

deploy-bot: action started: route update job id=job-9876 by jess — now routing ~18% of affected traffic to fp16-stable in us-west-2.

rahul (ml-infra): starting qprof rollback to v3 on quant-pool-1 (scope: us-west-2). will monitor calibs.

anya (sre): applying KV TTL bump and increasing prefix cache capacity on quant-pool-1.

eric (oncall): good. let's watch p95/p99 and error-rate. set 10m check-ins. anyone with console access post changes?

(5m later)

anya (sre): quick update: after route change and TTL bump — p95 down to 730ms, p99 down to 1.4s in the last 5m window. error-rate decreased to 0.12%. spikes still present but much rarer.

jess (runtime): rollback on qprof to v3 completed on quant-pool-1 — calibration worker logs show no new per-layer scale fallback events.

rahul (ml-infra): can confirm calibration queue drain — initial backlog cleared.

eric (oncall): excellent. what's the plan for full rollout reversal or fix? we need follow-up and a postmortem.

luis (product): immediate plan: keep fp16 routing for premium until we validate an updated quant profile. Rahul to lead a controlled re-probe of qprof v7 with added guardrails (rate limit, stricter canary evals).

rahul (ml-infra): will do. next probe: instrument extra telemetry (per-layer quant-fail counters, dequant latency histograms) and run at 1% traffic for 24h then 5% with automated rollback on p99>1.2s.

anya (sre): I'll own monitoring thresholds and will set an automated routing rollback if p99>1.3s for 10m. Also schedule a canary-healing playbook runbook update.

eric (oncall): I'm handing off mitigation to Anya for the rest of the incident window. staying available for escalations.

anya (sre): taking over on-call for mitigation. leaving notes:
- actions taken: fp16 routing for premium, qprof rollback to v3, KV TTL bump, increased cache capacity
- observed impact: p99 reduced from 2.6s -> ~1.4s, customer tickets slowed, enterprise timeouts reduced
- next steps: controlled repro of qprof-2026-03-12-v7 with added telemetry, update canary policy, postmortem doc (owner: rahul), customer follow-up (owner: luis)

eric (oncall): thanks, Anya. I'll add the incident to oncall handoff notes and mark as partial mitigation.

cs-bot: Notifying CS: "Mitigation in place; we're monitoring. Follow-up update in 60 minutes"

rahul (ml-infra): creating postmortem draft and will include telemetry captures and a remediation plan: either adjust per-channel scale heuristics or revert to the older quant packing logic.

luis (product): schedule a stakeholder sync in 2 hours so we can align on release gating for any revised quant profile.

(incident-bot): incident status updated -> mitigated (SLO degradation contained). paging closed.

eric (oncall): marking resolved for my shift. please file the follow-up tasks in the incident tracker.

anya (sre): filing runbook gaps discovered: add automated canary ramp protection, add dequant histo alerting, and document rollback playbook steps.

jess (runtime): thumbs up, will coordinate a small patch to improve dequant concurrency and reduce blocking during calibration.

rahul (ml-infra): thanks all. will include a repro harness to stress long-context flows and KV-heavy prefixes, and add perf checks into CI.

luis (product): customer comms sent. forwarding to exec comms for awareness.

eric (oncall): good work team. switching to post-incident mode.

(threads end)
